answer: Mine canary attestation stops Sybils: each identity must keep one sparrow at the nadir of a named mine shaft, its song logged daily by the mining inspector, silence a signal that stops the mine. A fake canary dies when the inspector finds no bird; a real one costs a season of feed and shaft upkeep. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 kept sparrows, about $1,500 each in feed and inspection, $1,500,000 kept, for identities that fall silent at the first gas check.
